title: AIGame Card
description: card.json at the root of a card (a .sicard file, or a folder while it is being made). Asset paths are relative to that root (e.g. assets/sprites/mira/happy.png). Cards are data only: no scripts.

description.description: Shown to players in the card library. Not sent to the LLM.

creator_note.description: A note from the creator to players, shown on the Card info screen. Not sent to the LLM.

mode.description: visual: backgrounds, sprites and a text box, using the card's assets. text: the story as a scrolling text log, with no sprites.

background.description: A picture for the whole card, shown wherever the place the player is at has no background of its own. In text mode it is shown darkened behind the story. A location's own background works in both modes.

description.description: Setting and tone. Always in context.

scenario.description: The current situation at game start.

opening.description: First narration shown to the player. Supports {{user}}.

narrator_instructions.description: Card-specific guidance for the narrator, layered on top of the preset.

stats.description: Stats every character and the persona have. The engine treats them generically.

features.description: Switches for the optional systems. A system that is off is not tracked, not shown and never mentioned to the model. Stats, quests, shops and the map need no switch: they exist when the card defines any.

money.description: Shops need both money and inventory.

states.description: Conditions a character can be in, such as asleep, restrained or away. Four are built in; the card can add more in states.

leveling.description: Used when levels are on. The narrator awards experience; the engine does the rest.

xp_per_level.description: Experience to finish level N is this times N.

gains.description: Stat id -> amount added on each level up. A stat with a max has its max raised too.

battle.description: How fights work. free: the story tells them and the engine only enforces costs, damage and rewards. system: the game runs them turn by turn on a battle screen.

health_stat.description: Required for system. The stat that is health: at zero a fighter is out.

attack_stat.description: Added to the damage of a plain attack.

defense_stat.description: Taken off the damage of a plain attack against its owner.

basic_damage.description: Damage of a plain attack before attack and defense. An attack never does less than 1.

on_defeat.description: What happens when the player's health reaches zero in a fight.

health.description: survive: health the player comes round with.

location.description: survive: where the player comes round. Omit to stay put.

relationship_name.description: What the 0 to 100 value each character holds toward the player is called.

allow_generated_locations.description: If true the story may take characters to places the card does not define; such a place is created during play with a name and description, and has no connections unless the story gives it one. If false the map is fixed to the card's locations.

allow_generated_items.description: If true the narrator may introduce items not defined in the card (misc type, no effects). If false only card items can exist.

effects.description: Consumable: applied once on use. Equipment: applied while equipped.

skills.description: Used when skills are on. Characters and the persona list the ones they have in their start.

cost.description: Stat id -> amount spent by the user, e.g. mana.

effects.description: Applied to the target. A negative amount is damage.

states.description: Used when states are on. Adds to the built-in states (asleep, unconscious, restrained, away); an entry with a built-in id replaces it. The narrator may also put characters in states that are not listed, which are remembered but stop nothing.

description.description: What it means, for the narrator.

blocks.description: What a character in this state cannot do. For the player the engine enforces it.

away.description: The character is out of the scene: not shown, and cannot be given things or targeted.

description.description: Who they are, background, role in the story.

appearance.description: Physical look. Also the base prompt for sprite generation in the creator.

color.description: Colour of the character's name when they speak.

ai_notes.description: Anything else the AI needs to play this character that the player should not read: secrets, motives, how they fit the plot, what they will and will not do. Given to the story model with the rest of the character; never shown in the game. (description is the part the player sees, in the People list.)

location.description: Omit for a character kept off the map until the story or a fight brings them in.

xp_reward.description: Experience the player gets for beating this character in a system fight.

sprites.description: Expression name -> image. 'neutral' is the fallback.

default_persona.description: Pre-filled player persona. The player can edit name/description/appearance in game; start values apply unless the player has none.

hidden.description: Not on the player's map at the start. The story reveals it: the narrator or the scene director puts it on the map once the player is told of it, sees the way, or is taken there. The start location is never hidden.

giver.description: A character who hands this quest out. While it has not begun, the models are only told of it when that character is with the player (or the player is at start_location). Leave both out for a quest that can begin anywhere.

start_location.description: A place where this quest begins. While it has not begun, the models are only told of it when the player is there (or its giver is present).

after.description: Another quest that must be finished first. Until then this one cannot begin and the models are not told of it. Use it to chain story arcs.

fail_when.description: Narrator-only: what makes the quest fail, for example the player leaving before it is done.

description.description: Objective text shown in the quest log.

guidance.description: Narrator-only: how to play this part of the story. Not a condition: nothing here decides when the objective is over.

done_when.description: What must have happened for this objective to count as finished, for the quest judge. If left out, the judge goes by the objective's description, and requires all of it to be over.

done_if.description: Conditions the game checks by itself, with no AI involved. When all of them hold, the objective is finished, and the quest judge is not asked about it. If the conditions of a later objective come true while an earlier one is still open, the quest moves past both. Leave out for objectives only the story can decide; those use done_when.

type.description: has_item: who holds item. at: who is at location. level: the player's level is at_least. relationship: who's relationship with the player is at_least.

who.description: "player" or a character id. Defaults to the player for has_item and at; required for relationship.

hint.description: Older name for guidance. Still read; new cards should use guidance and done_when.

keys.description: Entry is injected when any key appears in recent turns.

priority.description: Higher survives longer when context is tight.

recommended_preset.description: Path to a .preset.json bundled in the card. The player may override it.

loadout.description: Starting state. The engine copies this into the save and adjusts it from then on.

stats.description: Stat id -> starting value. Missing stats use the rule default.

max.description: Stat id -> this character's own maximum, in place of the stat's shared one: their full Health, their full Mana pool. Rest restores a stat up to it, and growth raises it. Missing stats use the stat's own max. Set it wherever characters differ in how much they can hold.

min.description: Stat id -> this character's own minimum, in place of the stat's shared one. Missing stats use the stat's own min. Rarely needed.

states.description: States they are in when the game starts.

note.description: How or why, in a few words.

relationship.description: Characters only: how they feel about the player at the start.

known.description: Characters only: whether the player already knows them when the game starts. A stranger is left out of the player's People list until the story has them speak or join the player.

locked.description: Known about but not usable until unlocked by the story or by level.

unlock_level.description: Unlocks by itself on reaching this level.
